title: jnprofile-typescript
text: jnprofile-typescript is the TypeScript profile of jnterfaces. A profile sets up a project in one language. It has tools, for example lint, and each tool brings its packages, its parts of the config files and its recipes. A recipe is a command of the project’s Justfile, such as just lint. The profile is for a TypeScript project with npm. The installer finds such a project by its package.json or tsconfig.json.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: Run this command in a project that has the jnterfaces installer: just install --profile typescript In a folder with no package.json, the command first runs npm init --yes. It then installs the tools lint and typecheck. If you do not choose other roles, it also turns on the default roles of the profile, tasker and prose. The section The roles of the jnterfaces guide says what each role installs. Then add or remove a tool: just install test just uninstall lint The machine needs just and uv. uv runs node and npm from the nodejs-wheel package, so you do not install node. To install every dependency into node_modules, run just setup.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: Tool Packages Recipes lint biome just fmt, just lint typecheck typescript, @types/node just typecheck test typescript, @types/node just build, just test The tools gives each recipe and each part that a tool adds to a config file.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: A part is the piece of a shared config file that a tool owns. just install adds the part, and just uninstall takes out only that part. Your own settings stay. A part is an include or a block of lines. biome.json and tsconfig.json get an include. The installer writes the settings of the profile to a file under .agents/config/typescript/, and adds that file to extends in your file. A setting in your file wins over the setting of the profile. When the project has a biome.jsonc and no biome.json, the include goes to biome.jsonc. .gitignore and .worktreedisposable get a block of lines. A block starts and ends with a comment that names its owner. Do not edit a file under .agents/config/. Only the installer writes these files. The section Shared files and the record of the jnterfaces guide says how the installer keeps a record of each part.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: jnterfaces: the installer, and the just, jagt-protocol and cx skills. jnprofile-python: the Python profile. agent_gest_git_skills: the tasker role and its g skills, the skills whose names start with g.

title: The tools
text: Each tool of the profile brings its packages, its recipes and its parts. The installer adds the packages to the devDependencies of package.json with npm.

title: The tools
text: Every project of the profile gets the base, even a project with no tool. Recipe What it does just setup Installs every dependency into node_modules, as package-lock.json says The recipes run node and npm with uvx --from 'nodejs-wheel==24.*'. The cache of npm is in .local/npm-cache. The base adds node_modules/, dist/, .local/ and *.tsbuildinfo to .gitignore. It adds node_modules/ and *.tsbuildinfo to .worktreedisposable. That file lists the ignored files that a command can make again. just worktrees-prune keeps a worktree that has ignored files, but it does not count these files.

title: The tools
text: The package is @biomejs/biome@2. Recipe What it does just fmt Formats the code. Extra arguments go to biome: just fmt src just lint Checks the code against the rules of biome. Extra arguments go to biome: just lint --write The part is an include in biome.json. Its extends names ./.agents/config/typescript/lint.json. That file makes biome read the ignore file of git, so biome skips the files that git ignores. It leaves out dist, node_modules, .agents, .claude and .codex. It also sets the formatter to indent with spaces and to keep lines to at most 120 characters.

title: The tools
text: The packages are typescript@7 and @types/node@24. Recipe What it does just typecheck Checks the types with tsc and tsconfig.json. A project in which tsconfig.json matches no code yet passes The part is an include in tsconfig.json. Its extends names ./.agents/config/typescript/tsconfig.json. That file compiles src/ into dist/ for ES2023 and NodeNext modules, in strict mode, with source maps and the types of node. Its paths start with ${configDir}, so they are paths in your project, not in .agents/config/.

title: The tools
text: The packages are typescript@7 and @types/node@24, as for typecheck. The tool has the same part in tsconfig.json. When both tools are on, the include stays until both are off. Recipe What it does just build Compiles the code into dist/, with tsconfig.json just test Compiles, then runs the tests in dist/ with node --test. With no arguments, a project in which tsconfig.json matches no code yet passes Put the code and the tests in src/. Name each test file NAME.test.ts, for example src/app.test.ts. The build writes it as dist/app.test.js. With no arguments, just test runs each file in dist/ whose name ends in .test.js. A test imports the code with the .js ending, for example import { add } from "./app.js", because the code runs from dist/.
